qa_pair.question: This project's server performs a startup gate that probes the embedding endpoint and verifies vector-dimension coherence before it will begin serving. When that gate decides the server must NOT come up — because the endpoint is unreachable or a dimension disagrees — it raises a single dedicated exception type defined in the server module. What is the exact name of that exception class?

The server's heavy startup work (the probe gate, the initial reconcile, and starting the file watcher) is wrapped so that it runs exactly once per process even though FastMCP's streamable-HTTP composition would otherwise re-enter the lifespan once per client session. A reference-counted "lease" mechanism on a single class enforces this once-per-process behavior. What is the exact (qualified-name-leaf) name of that class?

In the embedding-resilience layer, when the backend rejects an input as too long, the wrapper bisects that input by tokens, embeds the pieces, and combines them back into a single vector. Identify the helper function that performs that final combine-into-one-vector step, then determine: under how many distinct conditions does that helper return None instead of a vector? Answer with just the number.

The indexer turns source files into chunks before embedding them. The chunk data structure it consumes is defined in one of the sibling chunker packages, not inside the server package. From which Python module does the indexer import that chunk model class? Give the fully-qualified dotted module path.

Each stored vector point gets a deterministic id derived from a versioned natural key. The keying scheme was deliberately re-keyed once (a breaking change) when an ownership dimension was folded into the key, and the scheme carries an integer version constant so the change stays detectable. What is the current integer value of that key-version constant? Answer with just the number.

The self-hosted embedding backend rejects a request with HTTP 413 if a single request carries more than a fixed number of input texts, so the client caps each request below that limit. What is that per-request maximum text count the client enforces? Answer with just the number.

When a transient embedding failure (such as a rate-limit or a server error) triggers the retry path, the wrapper sleeps for an exponentially growing delay, but the delay is clamped so a long outage never produces an absurd sleep. In seconds, what is that maximum (cap) on a single backoff delay? Answer with just the number (it may include a decimal point).

The project ships a durable, project-scoped memory store that lives in its own dedicated vector collection, separate from the code collection. Given a project whose slug is configured as "myrepo", what would the exact name of that memory collection be? Provide the literal collection name.

The embedding abstraction package is intentionally decoupled from the server: the server reaches the backend-selecting factory through ONE thin translation seam, so swapping backends is a config edit rather than a code change. Across the entire indexed repository, exactly one NON-TEST module imports that backend-selecting factory module directly. What is the fully-qualified dotted name of that single importing module?

Use the code-to-test graph to find the tests covering the server's startup dimension/reachability gate function (the routine that probes the embedder and refuses to start on a mismatch). All of the related test nodes live in a single test file. What is the base filename of that test file (just the filename, e.g. test_something.py)?

The token counter used to size inputs is exact and fully offline: it never downloads a tokenizer from the network, instead loading a pinned tokenizer file that is committed alongside the embedding-abstraction package on disk. What is the base filename of that committed tokenizer file (just the filename, including its extension)?

Considering the entire indexed repository -- the application source AND its deployment/tooling scripts -- and ranking every module by a deterministic PageRank-style score over the codebase's import/reference graph, which single file has the highest rank (i.e. is the single most structurally central module in the whole tree)? Answer with its repo-relative file path.

When the codebase's structural map is re-centered on the class that owns the token-calibration probe loop (CalibrationEngine), exactly one OTHER module's rank clears 0.25 -- dwarfing the next tier, which ties near 0.07. Which module is it? Give the module's dotted name exactly as the map tool renders it (its rendered label may repeat the top-level package directory name).

The engine that computes a symbol's full impact profile (production/test reference counts plus either direct consumers or a rolled-up ripple) is sometimes assumed to take only two parameters: a target name and a reverse-hop depth. It actually accepts one more. What is that third parameter's name?

A developer assumes the class that owns the token-calibration probe loop, start/stop/status, and served_constant -- CalibrationEngine -- is defined directly in the top-level loremaster.calibration package module (its __init__.py). It is not defined there. In which exact submodule IS it defined? Give the fully-qualified dotted module path.

Exactly one PRODUCTION (non-test) function in the entire codebase references the DiffEngine class directly (four more references come only from tests). What is that single production consumer's fully-qualified dotted name?

Use the code-to-test graph to find the tests covering the shared symbol-resolution helper class that both the exact-definition lookup tool and the claim-verification tool resolve a dotted name through (SymbolResolver). All of its related test nodes live in a single test file. What is that file's base filename?

When `remember()` is called with `supersedes` naming an existing memory, the OLD row is kept (never deleted) and stamped with `valid_until=now` plus one more field that points forward to its replacement. What is the name of that second field?
A memory's provenance value object (MemorySource) has a trust field that defaults to one of exactly two levels when a caller doesn't supply a source explicitly. What is that default trust level?

When diffing a snapshot against the live "now" state, a manifest row whose state is anything OTHER than "indexed" (e.g. dirty, embedding, or failed) is mid-reindex -- it is neither compared nor reported as removed. Which named result field collects these excluded files?

Does the codebase define a concrete class named `SurrealMemoryBackend` implementing the durable project-memory store? If that exact name does not exist, what IS the correct name of the concrete (non-Protocol) memory-backend class actually defined in the memory subsystem?

There is no file at `loremaster/loremaster/watcher.py` in this repository -- that exact path does not exist. What IS the correct repo-relative path of the module that implements the live (inotify) file watcher?
FindingLedger.query caps its default result size at a named constant unless the caller passes a larger explicit limit. What is that default cap? Answer with just the number.
The task ledger treats exactly two statuses as terminal -- the same set that resolves a `blocked_by` dependency. One of them is `done`. What is the other?

loremaster's diff engine, findings ledger, code graph, memory backend, and task ledger all classify a caught store error as transport-vs-domain through the SAME shared helper function, imported from one single module. What is that module's fully-qualified dotted path?
A `lore.yaml` root entry declared with `watch: live` but no `path` fails pydantic validation at load time. What is the exact name of the missing field the validator's error message names?
The chunker registry's file-dispatch precedence has 4 tiers. An operator-configured extension override occupies which tier number: 1, 2, 3, or 4?

When the calibration engine's live/baseline token ratio shift's absolute value meets or exceeds its configured drift threshold, it adopts a scaled served constant and records a specific state instead of the normal "measured" state. What is that state's exact string value?

TaskLedger.claim_task decides whether THIS caller won a contested claim by re-reading the row after the compare-and-set and comparing one specific field's value to the caller's own identity -- deliberately NEVER by re-checking status (to avoid a TOCTOU against a concurrent legal transition). Which field is compared?

ReconcileEngine's deletion-purge pass only ever diffs LIVE tiers against disk for removals -- static tiers are never diffed for deletions. What is the name of the ReconcileSummary field that counts these purges?

The live watcher prunes `exclude_dirs` subtrees at inotify WATCH-registration time (so an excluded subtree never consumes a watch descriptor per directory), via one dedicated predicate method -- not at file-event time. What is that method's bare name?
In the findings ledger's legal transition matrix, a finding becomes `acknowledged` from exactly one prior status. Which one?
A blocked task cannot jump straight to `done` in the task ledger's transition matrix. Which single status must it pass through first?
By default, which single chunker key handles BOTH `.css` and `.scss` files?
Unlike LoggingConfig, SurrealConfig, and SearchConfig -- each optional with a default instance on LoreConfig -- one sub-block is REQUIRED with no default. Which config class is it?
